newsitem.title: USA: Former Mexican prosecutor jailed briefly.
newsitem.headline: Former Mexican prosecutor jailed briefly.

text.p: Former Mexican Deputy Attorney General Mario Ruiz Massieu, under U.S. house arrest for a year while fighting extradition and deportation, was jailed briefly on Tuesday by authorities who said he posed an increased flight risk, his attorney said.

Federal marshals arrested Ruiz Massieu on the grounds that a March 15 civil verdict in Houston, which found him guilty of taking millions of dollars in bribes from drug traffickers, "changed the circumstances" and made him more likely to flee, said his attorney Cathy Fleming.

But he was returned to house arrest after a brief hearing in Newark before U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service authorities, she said. Ruiz Massieu, wearing an electronic surveillance bracelet, has been staying at an undisclosed location in New Jersey.

The Houston jury said Ruiz Massieu took bribes from drug traffickers and stashed the money in a Texas bank, but also said he had not laundered the money and let him keep $1.1 million of a $9 million bank account seized two years ago by the U.S. government.
Ruiz Massieu testified the money was part of a family fortune and lavish bonuses paid to high-ranking government officials.
His attorney said he planned to appeal the verdict. She said her client felt he would be allowed to stay in the United States and had no reason to run.
The former top Mexican prosecutor was arrested on currency charges in March 1995 at Newark International Airport as he was about to board a plane for Spain with his wife and daughter.

The U.S. and Mexican governments have been trying unsuccessfully to have him extradited to Mexico on charges he embezzled funds and covered up an investigation into the September 1994 assassination of his brother, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, a leading member of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party.
In thwarting the U.S. and Mexican governments' extradition and deportation efforts, U.S. courts have found repeatedly that there was not enough evidence to support those charges.
Ruiz Massieu, who has applied for political asylum in the United States, has accused officials of trying to silence his criticism of the Mexican government.
He is awaiting an immigration hearing set for May 16.
